newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis last night warned unionists that major changes were in the pipeline to the welfare state and called on them to adjust their claims for increased wages, be more flexible in talks that could create new jobs and accept local wage agreements for economically depressed areas.
--The foreign ministry yesterday called Albanian claims that Greece was behind unrest to "liberate" the Greek minority "figments of the imagination".

--Athens greeted conciliatory comments from Turkey's chief of staff with reserve yesterday, saying it would await "appropriate initiatives which will show that they are not words without substance". Later in the day, the response was provided by the violations of Greek airspace by Turkish fighter planes.

--Taxation offices will remain open until 8 p.m. every evening until the Friday deadline for submission of tax declarations. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said yesterday a new extension was not considered necessary, but staff say more than 1.5 million wage-earners and pensioners have yet to submit their declarations, due tomorrow.

--The claims from the former head of the Albanian secret services that Greece is behind the uprising in the south - where the majority of the ethnic Greek minority lives - were calmly but firmly dismissed by Athens.

--Reports state that the finance ministry is considering "an extension on the quiet" to the deadline for tax submissions through to early next week, after seeing the queues of taxpayers at local offices and the myriad mistakes on forms.
--Veteran Communist Harilaos Florakis will undergo surgery today for a stomach complaint.
--A new book on the life of Aristotle Onassis has brought denials from the Onassis Foundation and claims that the writer was never a confidante of the late shipping tycoon.
--Leading physicians have condemned unnecessary bypass surgery, saying that more than 2,000 operations a year put patients' lives at risk needlessly.

--New conservative opposition New Democracy leader Costas Karamanlis officially took over the reins of the party yesterday and is expected to have talks with leading party members as he chooses his advisers.
--Changes in pensions are in the pipeline, including new limits on the retirement age in the public sector and banks. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
